extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and academic institutions seeking funding from the Volkswagen Foundation (especially in the humanities, social sciences, and German higher-education institutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Volkswagen Foundation's funding portfolio: priority profile areas, example funding programmes, eligible applicants, types of funding, aims, and application timing. Useful for researchers and institutions assessing fit and preparing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile area — Societal Transformations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expanding knowledge about processes of transformation and developing possible courses of action together with stakeholders in civil society. Indicates funding priority for projects that engage with social change and co-develop actionable approaches with non-academic stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile area — Exploration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking into previously unexplored research territory with unconventional ideas and experimental approaches. Signals support for high-risk, high-gain, exploratory/basic research that departs from conventional methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile area — Understanding Research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically exploring and reflecting on the research system with a view to initiating positive change on areas such as career paths, governance, research and teaching. Targets meta-research and projects aimed at improving research structures and practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile area — zukunft.niedersachsen
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding programme for top-level research in Lower Saxony. A regional priority area focused on strengthening research excellence in Lower Saxony (Niedersachsen).

rubrics_metrics.name: General funding focus
rubrics_metrics.description: We support future-oriented topics with our funding offers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation prioritises projects that address forward-looking, future-relevant research questions and structural measures. Applicants should highlight the future relevance and long-term impact of their proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing — rolling vs deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications can be submitted at any time / specific deadline dates for other programmes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some programmes (e.g., Transatlantic Bridge Professorships) accept applications at any time, while others have fixed deadlines. Applicants must check each programme's timeline and note available online Q&As and information events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transatlantic Bridge Professorships — eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding programme for professors in the humanities and social sciences currently working in the USA who wish to work both in the USA and in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area of research: Humanities and Social Sciences. Type of funding: proportional financing of a professorship. Rolling applications possible. Targeted at professors with ties to both the USA and Germany; suited to proposals that plan transatlantic academic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: zukunft.niedersachsen — Lower Saxony Impulse Professorship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Lower Saxony Impulse Professorship' addresses academics approaching the end of their early career phase up to a maximum of ten years after completing their doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed for early-career academics (up to 10 years post-PhD). Check programme website for specific requirements and deadlines. Regional focus: Lower Saxony.

rubrics_metrics.name: zukunft.niedersachsen — Boost Research! Seed Grants objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Boost Research! Seed Grants for Lower Saxony
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This funding programme offers researchers the opportunity to receive seed funding for novel collaborative projects. The aim is to use the funding to enable the acquisition of additional third-party funding. Regional focus: Lower Saxony; meant to leverage further external funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researching Research: Strengthening University Centres — target and funding type
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding offer is aimed at established centres, institutes or research priority areas for Science Studies at universities in Germany that have been institutionalised in recent years and are striving for further structural development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type of funding: funds for structural measures. Eligibility: university-based centres/institutes in Germany focused on Science Studies seeking organisational/structural development. Online Q&As provided; intended to strengthen institutional capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pioneering Research — Exploring the Unknown Unknown — eligibility and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding offer addresses outstanding post-doctoral researchers and professors universities and research institutes in Germany, international cooperation partners are possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Area of research: all disciplines. Type of funding: visionary projects from the field of basic research. Targets outstanding researchers (postdocs and professors) undertaking visionary/basic research; international partners may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Experimental Spaces — university development scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Impetus for the German Science System: Strategic Experimental Spaces – University Development Requires Flexibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation invites universities, in conjunction with the relevant ministries, to open and design experimental spaces to test new forms of cross-border or cross-institutional cooperation. Type of funding: strategic projects. Aimed at universities and ministries; calls and formats may be modified over time (e.g., task forces, collaborative projects under evaluation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformational Knowledge on Democracies under Change — transdisciplinary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The programme addresses persons from science together with actors outside of academia who are interested in transdisciplinary research and aim at jointly developing new perspectives on democratic forms of government under change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Areas of research: humanities, cultural and social sciences (lead); cooperation with natural, life, data and technical sciences possible. Type of funding: task forces, cooperation projects. Emphasises collaboration between academic and non-academic actors and transdisciplinary methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opus Magnum — target audience and funding type
rubrics_metrics.description: Opus Magnum — The funding offer is aimed at outstanding professors from the humanities and social sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type of funding: funding of a substitute professorship. Intended for distinguished humanities and social sciences professors; consult detailed programme page for eligibility, scope, and deadlines.
